summary: The packet is a faithful, well-closed decomposition of Serre's deduction (Théorème 4, §4.6) of modularity of E/ℚ from the classical Serre theorem, organised under the accepted RS-06. Its mathematics survives attack: the conductor criteria, the witnesses at level N, the norm argument, exact conductor, local factors in Mathlib's convention, the root number and the concrete tests are all right. Five findings. (1, medium, duplicate) The review-added lemma strong-multiplicity-one-across-levels re-plans a named target of the Tau Ceti ModularForms roadmap: Layer 5's 'Cross-level strong multiplicity one, for newforms (Miyake Thm 4.6.19)', which the reviewed audit lists as that layer's target. §15 forbids re-planning a Tau Ceti roadmap. (2, low) Seven nodes use suppliers they request (ModularForms Layers 4, 7 and 8g, EllipticCurves Layer 4, JacobianChallenge Layer F) without listing them as prerequisites, nine pairs in all. The stage edges exist anyway. (3, low) The (ii)⇒(i) step writes V_r(J₀(N)) ≅ ⊕_f ⊕_λ V_{f,λ} without old-form multiplicities, which is false already at N = 22. (4, low) The three exceptional-set tests would not catch a definition that drops the isogeny and j-invariant clauses, or one that includes extra primes. (5, low) The suggested Lean file contains none of the packet's twelve unit tests; eight of its sixteen API items are absent, and several others appear only in comments. Its reason, that newforms are not in the pinned libraries, is contradicted by the packet's own baseline citation of HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.

Read all six stage descriptions R29.1–R29.6 and the accepted RS-06 (data/restructure/RS-06.result.json): its layer decisions for R29.1–R29.6 and R28.6, and its owners table. The packet follows RS-06's ownership: End_ℚ(E) = ℤ goes to R28.6, fixed-level strong multiplicity one to ModularForms Layer 5, the Weierstrass local polynomial and L-series to Mathlib, and A_f to R14.5.

Serre 1987 (Collège de France PDF, SHA-256 8048919d…e038, matching the packet), §4.6–4.7, pp. 207–209, read in full. Every Serre excerpt the packet uses is literal in the text layer: Lemme 5, the conditions (a)/(b) with Serre's 'si p > 5, on vérifie', 'ce qui d'ailleurs suffirait pour la suite', the lifting and pigeonhole passage, (4.6.4), Remarque (2) on primitivity, and Théorème 5. Carayol 1986, Faltings 1983, Deligne–Serre 1974 and Cremona were not re-read; their excerpts were checked only for consistency with the node statements.

Mathematics checked node by node. residual-conductor-divides: the tame inequality and the wild Swan comparison, using that a pro-ℓ image in GL₂(ℤ_p) injects mod p. residual-conductor-equality: the Tate-curve criterion at multiplicative ℓ, and at additive ℓ the potentially-good inertia image of order dividing 24 and the ramified quadratic character in the potentially multiplicative case, so p ≥ 5 suffices and the extension of Serre's p > 5 to p = 5 is sound. The witness level: N(ρ̄) | M | N forces the newform level to be N. The trivial-nebentypus lemma: the order of ε divides φ(N). strong-multiplicity-one-across-levels, exact-conductor via Carayol, and bad-euler-factors: split multiplicative 1 − T gives A_ℓ = +1, nonsplit 1 + T gives −1, additive gives 0. The root number w = eigenvalue of −W_N, from Λ(f,s) = (−1)^{k/2}η Λ(f,k−s) at k = 2. Manin's constant for the optimal quotient.

Concrete tests recomputed with exact rational arithmetic. 11a1, y² + y = x³ − x² − 10x − 20: (5,5) has order 5, Δ = −11⁵, v₁₁(j) = −5, a₂ = −2, so Σ = {2, 3, 5, 11}. 26b1, y² + xy + y = x³ − x² − 3x + 3: (1,0) has order 7, Δ = −2⁷·13, v₂(j) = −7. Standard facts also check: S₂(Γ₀(11)) and S₂(Γ₁(11)) are one-dimensional, 11a1 = X₀(11) has modular degree 1, the 5-isogeny 11a1 → 11a3 gives degree 5, 37a1 has modular degree 2, and w = +1 for 11a1.

Baseline: all 16 declarations exist at Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 (baseline index). Read in full: WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial (LFunction.lean:43: minimal model; a = q + 1 − #W′(κ); 1 − X, 1 + X, 1 for split, nonsplit and additive reduction), LFunction (:79, the Euler product over HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) of adic-completion local factors) and LSeries (:84); HeckeRing.GL2.Newform (Newform.lean:102, with level N, weight k and a nebentypus field χ); eq_of_forall_notMem_eigenvalue_eq (StrongMultiplicityOne.lean, fixed level and nebentypus only). Neither library has a conductor of an elliptic curve.

findings.claim: The packet plans, as its own lemma node, cross-level strong multiplicity one for weight-two, trivial-character newforms of levels dividing N. This is a named target of an existing Tau Ceti roadmap, stated there in greater generality: ModularForms Layer 5 plans 'Cross-level strong multiplicity one, for newforms (Miyake Thm 4.6.19)' for newforms of any levels N, M and the same weight, with equal level, equal nebentypus and equality as conclusion. PROTOCOL §15 says a Tau Ceti roadmap is never re-planned; its layers are cited as prerequisites. The node's hypotheses cite only the fixed-level library theorem and an audit of Layer 4, and never mention that Layer 5 owns the cross-level statement. Its proof plan re-derives the theorem from an Atkin–Lehner–Li decomposition requested from Layer 4. RS-06 already moved fixed-level strong multiplicity one from R29.3 to ModularForms Layer 5, and the cross-level form belongs with it.
findings.evidence: ModularForms Layer 5 stage description (data/atlas.json, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-5-strong-multiplicity-one-and-the-eigenform-characterization): 'Cross-level strong multiplicity one, for newforms (Miyake Thm 4.6.19): two normalized newforms f, g of the same weight and of levels N, M whose eigenvalues a_p agree at all but finitely many primes p ∤ NM satisfy N = M, have the same nebentypus, and are equal. … it is a named target of this layer.' Its document (content/tau-ceti/ModularForms/README.md, line 1427) reads 'Layer 5 (fixed-space SMO; multiplicity one; newform–newform cross-level SMO)'. The reviewed audit (data/library-coverage.json, that layer) lists the target 'Cross-level strong multiplicity one for newforms (Miyake 4.6.19) …' as library 'absent'. The packet node states 'Let f and g be normalised newforms of weight 2 and trivial character, of levels M and M′ dividing N. If A_ℓ(f) = A_ℓ(g) for all but finitely many primes ℓ ∤ N, then M = M′ and f = g', with prerequisites only tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.Newform and tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.eq_of_forall_notMem_eigenvalue_eq. RS-06 owners: 'Fixed-level/fixed-nebentypus strong multiplicity one …' has owner ModularForms Layer 5, formerly EllipticCurveModularity:R29.3.

findings.claim: PROTOCOL §3 requires every named fact a step uses to be listed as a prerequisite, and for a cross-roadmap need, the supplier stage listed alongside its requests entry. In this packet the requests' neededBy fields name the consuming nodes, but those nodes do not list the supplier. There are nine such pairs. EllipticCurves Layer 4 (Tate curve) is missing from residual-conductor-equality and bad-euler-factors. ModularForms Layer 4 (finiteness of newforms, newform decomposition) is missing from a-single-newform, newform-of-E and bad-euler-factors. ModularForms Layer 8g (Galois conjugates of newforms) is missing from rational-coefficient-field. JacobianChallenge Layer F (Abel–Jacobi) is missing from modular-parametrisation. ModularForms Layer 7 (Hecke's continuation and functional equation) is missing from l-function-continuation. The node-level dependency graph therefore does not close as §3 states. The stage-level edges already exist in the production graph, so no atlas link is lost.

For example, the ModularForms Layer 7 request 'Analytic continuation and functional equation of L(f, s) for a weight-two newform with trivial character' has neededBy [R29.6/l-function-continuation], whose prerequisites are ['EllipticCurveModularity:R29.4/bad-euler-factors', 'mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.LFunction', 'mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.LSeries'], and whose proof step reads 'Continuation and functional equation of L(F_E, s) are Hecke's theorem (Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 7).' findings.fix: Add the supplier stage id to each of the nine prerequisite lists named above. After finding 1, add the ModularForms Layer 5 stage wherever uniqueness across levels is used.

findings.claim: The step asserts 'V_r(J₀(N)) ≅ ⊕_f ⊕_{λ|r} V_{f,λ} (R19.6)' with f running over newforms of level dividing N. That drops the old-form multiplicities and is false for every N that has proper old spaces. The correct decomposition counts each newform f of level M | N with multiplicity σ₀(N/M), the number of divisors of N/M. The conclusion drawn, that the semisimple quotient V_r(E) is isomorphic to some V_{f,λ}, is unaffected, since Jordan–Hölder only needs the set of constituents.
findings.evidence: N = 22: X₀(22) has genus 2, so V_r(J₀(22)) has ℚ_r-dimension 4. S₂(Γ₀(22))^new = 0, S₂(Γ₀(2)) = 0, and the only newform of level dividing 22 is the level-11 form, whose V_{f,r} has dimension 2. The packet's own acceptance example in strong-multiplicity-one-across-levels records that S₂(Γ₀(22)) has dimension 2, spanned by f(z) and f(2z) with no new part. The step reads: '(ii) ⇒ (i): V_r(E) is then a Galois quotient of V_r(J₀(N)) ≅ ⊕_f ⊕_{λ|r} V_{f,λ} (R19.6); V_r(E) being semisimple (R28.6), Jordan–Hölder gives V_r(E) ≅ V_{f,λ} …'.
findings.fix: Write V_r(J₀(N)) ≅ ⊕_{M|N} ⊕_{f new of level M} (⊕_{λ|r} V_{f,λ})^{⊕σ₀(N/M)}, or say only that every Jordan–Hölder constituent of V_r(J₀(N)) is some V_{f,λ} with f new of level dividing N. Check that the requested R19.6 statement is stated with these multiplicities.

findings.claim: §12 asks for unit tests that a plausible wrong definition fails. None of the three tests exercises the two substantive clauses of Σ_E above 5, the rational-isogeny clause and the v_ℓ(j_E) clause, and none tests non-membership. A definition that drops both clauses, or one that adds any finite set of extra primes, passes all three. The only prime above 5 tested is 11 ∈ Σ_{11a1}, and that comes from the bad-reduction clause.
findings.evidence: The tests read: '5 ∈ Σ_E (rational 5-torsion) and 11 ∈ Σ_E' for 11a1 (5 is already in Σ because p ≤ 5); '2, 3, 5 ∈ Σ_E for every E'; 'Σ_E is still finite; 2 ∈ Σ_E' for y² = x³ − x. My exact computation: 11a1 has Δ = −11⁵, v₁₁(j) = −5, and a point of order 5, so Σ_{11a1} = {2, 3, 5, 11} and 7 ∉ Σ_{11a1}. 26b1 (y² + xy + y = x³ − x² − 3x + 3, conductor 26) has the rational point (1, 0) of order 7, Δ = −2⁷·13 and v₂(j) = −7, so 7 ∈ Σ_{26b1} although 7 > 5 and 7 ∤ 26.
findings.fix: Add two tests. exceptionalPrimes_11a1_seven: 7 ∉ Σ_{11a1}, a non-membership test that catches over-inclusive definitions. exceptionalPrimes_26b1: 7 ∈ Σ_{26b1}, caused by the rational 7-torsion point (1, 0) and by 7 | v₂(j) = −7, which catches definitions dropping those clauses. Put both in the suggested file under these names.
